name: Lexware Office (formerly lexoffice)
tagline: Cloud bookkeeping, invoicing and tax filing for German freelancers and small businesses.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The invoicing screen is the easy part: line items, VAT rates, a PDF, a number sequence. The part you cannot one-shot is everything downstream of it: GoBD-compliant immutable records with an audit trail, ELSTER submissions for Umsatzsteuer-Voranmeldung and EÜR, DATEV exports your tax advisor will actually accept, and bank transaction sync via licensed account access. Those are regulated interfaces with certification, credentials and liability attached, not REST endpoints you discover on a weekend. A self-built ledger also means you personally own the answer when a Betriebsprüfer asks why invoice 2024-0043 changed. Build the invoice generator if you want, keep the bookkeeping where someone else carries the compliance risk.
coreLoopDIY: A local invoice and expense ledger with gap-free numbering, VAT totals, PDF output and a CSV export you hand to your tax advisor.
requirements: Node 20+ and a machine you back up
Chromium for PDF rendering via Puppeteer
Your own VAT logic sanity-checked by an actual tax advisor
Manual bank statement CSV imports, no account access API
whatYouLose: ELSTER filing: no VAT returns or EÜR submitted from your own app
GoBD-grade immutability and audit trail that survives a tax audit
DATEV / tax advisor handoff in a format they expect
Automatic bank sync and payment matching
Ongoing updates when German VAT rules, e-invoicing mandates or XRechnung specs change
moatNotes: German bookkeeping software is mostly a compliance wrapper with a UI attached. The UI is the cheap half.
whyPeopleStillPay: People pay because the invoice PDF is not the product, the legally defensible paper trail is. Lexware Office keeps records in a form the Finanzamt accepts, pushes VAT returns through ELSTER, hands clean data to a Steuerberater, and pulls bank transactions in through licensed account access. If the rules change, and in Germany they change, someone else ships the update. A personal build gives you invoices; it does not give you someone to blame.
notes: You can absolutely build the invoice generator in an afternoon and it will look better than theirs. The moat is ELSTER, GoBD and DATEV: three regulated handshakes that do not care how nice your UI is.
prompt:
Build a local-first invoicing and expense ledger for a single German freelancer. No accounts, no cloud, no telemetry.

Stack, non-negotiable:
- Next.js 15 App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, file at ./data/ledger.db
- Puppeteer for PDF rendering from an HTML invoice template
- Zod for validation, no ORM beyond hand-written SQL helpers

Data model:
- clients: name, address lines, country, VAT id (optional)
- invoices: gap-free sequential number in format YYYY-NNNN, issue date, service period, client ref, status (draft, issued, paid, cancelled), currency EUR only
- invoice_items: description, quantity, unit price in cents, VAT rate (0, 7, 19)
- expenses: date, vendor, gross amount in cents, VAT rate, category, optional receipt file path

Rules to enforce in code:
- money is integer cents everywhere, never floats
- an invoice with status issued becomes read-only: edits are blocked, corrections happen via a cancellation entry plus a new invoice
- invoice numbers are assigned only on issue, inside a transaction, never reused
- append-only audit_log table: timestamp, entity, entity id, action, JSON diff

Screens:
- invoice list with status filter and yearly totals
- invoice editor with live net / VAT / gross breakdown per rate
- one-click PDF render to ./data/invoices/YYYY-NNNN.pdf
- expense list with monthly totals grouped by VAT rate
- export page: CSV of invoices, invoice items and expenses for a chosen year, plus a plain VAT summary per rate

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt or fake:
- ELSTER submission, DATEV export formats, XRechnung / ZUGFeRD generation
- bank account sync or payment matching
- any claim of GoBD compliance

Seed the database with two clients and three example invoices. Put any config in .env with a .env.example committed. README must state in the first paragraph that this is a personal ledger, not certified bookkeeping software, and that filings still go through a tax advisor.
